key_insight: Coordinating LLM actions across paired simulations reduces finite-difference gradient variance from O(c⁻²) to O(c⁻¹), while first-switch conditioning keeps it bounded under suitable stability conditions.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables more reliable gradient-based policy optimization in operational simulators with black-box, LLM-driven human decisions.
method: Maximally couple LLM action distributions to minimize action switches while preserving each simulation’s behavioral law.
Condition on the first switch to average over whether it occurs and control gradient variance.
Use an impact-aware extension to prioritize influential switches.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthesized and LLM-embedded simulators support the variance theory and show substantial performance gains; the paper also establishes improved complexity bounds for projected stochastic approximation.
watch_item: Bounded variance requires suitable stability conditions, and implementation must support coupling the LLM action distributions.
paper_title: Gradient Estimation for LLM-Embedded Simulation Optimization
